ButtonUnmask.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    remaining_target_positions
        With empty incoming memory, read the requested cube colors in goal order and write their visible initial [y, x] positions as an ordered list. Otherwise carry the incoming list unchanged unless the observed execution shows a previously resting container at the first listed position being grasped and lifted, with that container now held and its cube exposed; then remove that first entry. Require a new resting-to-held transition: a container already held at the beginning of a put-down execution must not trigger another removal. Do not remove an entry merely because a pickup is being selected, and do not restore entries after release. Preserve stored coordinates rather than updating them from shifted visible-pixel centers. e.g. [[92, 93], [128, 118]]

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    Start each episode with A, press the button: the initial scene shows uncovered cubes, no held container, and no completed press in the observed execution. After the observed execution shows the hand descending onto the button and withdrawing, choose B if no container is held and remaining_target_positions is nonempty. Explicit 'pressed down' text is not required; the low hand contacting the button followed by withdrawal also establishes the press. For B, select the resting container covering the first stored position, using the covering event when visible or the nearest resting container to that position otherwise. Classify the side from which it approaches, not the direction of motion: motion toward smaller x from larger x is insertion from robot-left, not robot-right. These labels are robot-relative, not camera-relative. If the peg disappears into the box, use the last clearly visible approach before occlusion, not the final occluded frame. Ignore the original pickup location, the high transport path (including any crossing over the box), and the reset execution scene when assigning the side. Write this value at the first decision.     pre_press_target
        Despite its legacy name, this field holds the goal-selected demonstration target. For 'right after', follow its next transfer and find its first completed target placement after the press; merely remaining on the old target immediately after button contact is not a new placement. Use release and subsequent resting evidence to identify the placement, allowing occlusion. Use the selected demonstration placement to identify the physical target, then follow that target through all subsequent demonstration frames to execution start, including shuffles, exchanges, crossings, and temporary occlusion. Resolve identity using the observed motion sequence and joint continuity of moving targets; do not assume spatial rank or target-list order identifies it, or independently match the final scene to its original position. Write exactly that physical target's reported execution-start center as [y, x], not its earlier demonstration center, the released cube's center, or the center of another target now occupying its former position. Ignore later placements when selecting the target, but continue tracking the selected target's subsequent motion. If its physical identity cannot be resolved, write "unknown". Once populated, copy the incoming value unchanged at every decision step; do not replace it with the cube's current position or a newly shifted visible centroid. If no target can be identified, write "unknown". e.g. [126, 145]
